settings.heading: Start at the contact patch.
settings.image_alt: Racing slick tires in a pit garage
settings.body:
The right tire starts with how and where you drive. Before comparing compounds, establish the dimensions and requirements of your car and wheels.

Know your dimensions

Record the full tire size, wheel diameter and width. Check the tire manufacturer’s approved rim-width range, load requirements and clearance information for your exact application.

Match the intended use

Check whether the tire is intended for dry track use, wet conditions or road use. A racing slick should not be assumed to be road legal or suitable for standing water.

Use the manufacturer’s setup guidance

Pressure targets, heat cycles and storage requirements vary by tire. Use the current instructions for the exact model, and record conditions and pressures with your installer or track support team.

settings.heading: Think in systems.
settings.image_alt: Red racing brake caliper and steel rotor
settings.body:
A caliper is one part of a matched system. Vehicle model alone is not enough to confirm that a brake component will fit.

Confirm the application

Check the vehicle year, model, trim, axle position and existing brake package. Record the manufacturer’s part number and any modifications to the car.

Check dimensions and clearance

Rotor diameter and thickness, hat offset, mounting brackets, pad shape and wheel clearance all matter. Where supplied, use the manufacturer’s wheel-clearance template before ordering.

Plan the complete installation

Confirm the required hardware, fluid compatibility and installation procedure with the component supplier. Have the system installed and checked by a qualified professional, following the exact product instructions.

settings.heading: Arrive with a plan.
settings.image_alt: Close-up of textured racing tire rubber
settings.body:
A clear preparation routine helps you arrive ready to focus. Keep a record of the parts fitted to your car and the instructions that accompany them.

Review before the event

Check the event organiser’s vehicle requirements and inspection process. Arrange a pre-event inspection with a qualified workshop and follow the relevant component service guidance.

Bring the right information

Keep tire and brake specifications, installation records and supplier contacts together. Note any fitment changes since the last event.

Inspect and record

Use manufacturer guidance for inspection limits, bedding procedures and maintenance. Record observations between sessions and ask a qualified professional to investigate unusual wear, vibration or changes in braking performance.
